chunk_map.heading: You steer the answer by loading context

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an unresolved referent strands the reader mid-slide. Chunk 1 (3-9): 'the first prompt' (5,7), 'it runs'/'Claude suggest' (7), and 'the first exchange'/'context colored everything after' (9) all resolve inside the same chunk against 'Two Claude Code sessions' (5) and the two named prompts. Chunk 2 (11-15): line 13 'Context is whatever you tell it' — 'it' = Claude, named four times in chunk 1, a term introduced on an earlier slide and reused, the compendium's explicit NOT-a-violation case; line 15 'The move is loading the right context before the question' restates the chunk's own header (11) and the 'dinner question' narrated in chunk 1 — within-file continuation, not a dangling pointer. No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent in the current 2-chunk body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reveal narrated before its guess kills the demo's payoff. Chunk 1 (3-9): guess at line 7 ('Take a guess before it runs. What does Claude suggest now?') precedes the reveal at line 9 ('Something Finnish: salmon, rye bread, meatballs.') — correct order, same chunk. Matches the maintainer block's own accept-note (L21: 'Guess before reveal. The guess paragraph precedes the Finnish-dinner answer. Both sessions get narrated before the live run.').

Harm: a chunk whose only content is a wait-state or one context-dependent bullet says nothing standalone. Chunk 1 (3-9) carries the full two-session demo plus reveal; chunk 2 (11-15) carries the steering claim and its restatement. Chunk 0 is the title-only H1 with no lede, the standard title-slide shape (matches maintainer standing constraint 'Openers carry no setup lede'), not the wait-state/context-dependent-bullet failure this rule targets.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a header-only skim. 'Context is King' (chunk 1) is delivered exactly: the same second question gets two different answers depending on what came before. 'You steer the answer by loading context' (chunk 2) is restated near-verbatim at line 15 ('The move is loading the right context before the question'). Both headers are true summaries of their own chunk.

Checked all six sub-patterns against the body (lines 1-15): (1) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple — none; (2) anaphora/epistrophe triples — none; (3) self-grading superlatives — none (grep -inE 'one of the (most|best)' -> 0 hits); (4) number + own retraction — body prose contains zero digits (grep -noE '[0-9]+' on lines 1-15 -> no matches); (5) abstraction-noun stacks — body stays concrete throughout (capital of Italy, pasta/osso buco/risotto, largest lake in Finland, salmon/rye bread/meatballs); (6) verb triplets with an empty leg — none. No sub-item hit, no self-grading-superlative instance either, so no blocking value-prop-leak.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content present in long-read but absent from the composed deck silently strands a reader who toggled to Slides. Ran: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md -> 'files: 1  slides: 2' — matches the file's 2 '##' chunks exactly, confirming both sections reach buildDeckModel. This is a straightforward lecture body under the standard .phase--lecture wrapper (no phase-less prework/supplementary block that could be silently dropped, the 2026-07-09 failure mode).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a label-shaped header on a lecture wastes the beat where a law should be named. This file is a lecture, so headings owe claims: 'Context is King' (a maxim/claim) and 'You steer the answer by loading context' (a claim about reader agency) — both claims, neither a bare label nor a phase tag. Classified non-blocking per the template's stated principle (postdates the explicit rules 1/2/3/4/8/10/12 blocking list): a label-shaped header would cost the reveal-a-law beat, not comprehension, consistent with header-adjacent rule 6's non-blocking status. No violation present either way.
